 Shri Anupam Chaturvedi - Panel Lawyer for the responde
 Order

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.238/2024 registered at Police Station-Kamarji, District- Sidhi (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(1) of IPC, Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(va) of SC & ST (POA) Act, 1989.

The applicant is in custody since 23.08.2024.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the victim has not supported the prosecution case.
In paragraph no.6 of her statement, she has stated that her maternal uncle's home is in Hardua and she went to study in Hardua from Class-I and II.
Subsequently, she was admitted in Class-I of Patpara school and his father has mentioned her date of birth on estimation.
She has denied that the applicant has committed rape upon her.

Her mother has partially supported the prosecution case in the cross-examination but she NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50760 2 MCRC-41724-2025 has also admitted that her daughter was born in 2006.

She has also admitted in paragraph no.10 of her cross-examination that her daughter was born in the hospital but she did not remember her date of birth and she has no knowledge about the fact that her birth certificate was issued by the hospital or not.

She has also admitted that for the primary education for Class-I and II, the victim went to study in Hardua, District-Katni then she was admitted in Patpara Government School and her date of birth in the school record was recorded by her husband on the basis of estimation.
The same fact has also been admitted by the father of the victim (PW-3) in paragraph no.4 of his cross-examination.
On that basis, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that DNA report is uninterpretable.
It is clear that the victim was major at the time of incident, hence, the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that the date of birth of the victim is 21.07.2006.
On that basis, on the date of incident, she was minor and her parents have clearly supported the prosecution case, hence, no case of bail is made out.

4. Heard the parties and perused the case diary.
5.

Looking to the age of the victim and the factual aspects of the case that the date of birth is disputed and DNA report is uninterpretable, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50760 3 MCRC-41724-2025 of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during pendency of trial.
7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
8. Accordingly, Misc. Criminal Case stands disposed of.
C.c. as per rules.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE HK Vinay Patel vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40718416/
